rationale: Attempt: use background 8 and directional nearest-colour context. The rule rotates each 6's displacement around its paired 1; these keys omit the distances needed to locate the new 7.

Attempt: learn object recolouring by pixel count. The intended colour depends on the separate blue symbol's shape, which none of the available per-object properties can communicate to the grey object.

Attempt: use eight-neighbour counts to capture more corridor corners. Filling depends on corridor connectivity and whether the 9 blocks passage; identical local neighbourhoods can require different outputs.
Attempt: enable colour 8 as a source, preserving cardinal rays in source colours. The template cannot assign colour 2 specifically at intersections while retaining source colours elsewhere.

Attempt: replace absolute modulo coordinates with full local patterns. In the first demonstration, pixels (1,2) and (1,3), indexed from zero, have identical 3x3 input patterns but require 8 and 2. The other key kinds also cannot distinguish the required shape decomposition.
Attempt: use full 3x3 patterns for richer boundary context. Completing each object's bounding rectangle requires component-specific extents, which the available pixel keys do not encode.

Attempt: use union to include both shared and unmatched positions. The rule preserves shared colours and assigns distinct colours to first-only and second-only cells; this template emits only one nonzero colour.

Attempt: reduce retention to favour demonstrated clearing of old red positions. Every pixel of a given input colour receives the same output colour, so the template cannot translate a shape or selectively create red pixels on background.
Attempt: switch enclosure detection to eight-connectivity. The template fills all enclosed background with one learned colour; it cannot generate the required alternating 2 and 4 spiral.

Attempt: use full local patterns to distinguish more interior and exterior configurations. The rule colours background components by their connectivity to the grid border, which none of these pixel keys represents.
